findings.title: Callable object parameter types crash during command definition
findings.cause: FuncParamType accepts a Callable but unconditionally reads func.__name__ to populate self.name. Callable instances that implement __call__ commonly do not define __name__, and convert_type forwards explicit non-built-in callable objects to FuncParamType.
findings.impact: A Click command using a callable instance as an option or argument type raises AttributeError while decorators build the command, so the CLI module can fail to import before any invocation or user-facing error handling runs.
evidence: src/click/types.py:185-188 defines FuncParamType.__init__(func: Callable[[Any], T]) and assigns self.name = func.__name__.
src/click/types.py:1249-1259 sends explicit non-ParamType, non-builtin type values to FuncParamType(guessed).
src/click/core.py:2182 converts the public Parameter type argument with types.convert_type(type, default) while constructing parameters.
A direct runtime probe defining @click.option('--value', type=UpperCase()) where UpperCase implements __call__ failed with: AttributeError 'UpperCase' object has no attribute '__name__'.
